# Contributing

Eyas doesn't accept code contributions or pull requests from outside the project. Every change is written and reviewed by the maintainer, so there's no third-party code to audit for security. Pull requests from others will be closed without review.

Ideas, suggestions and feedback are very welcome, and they're how the project decides what to build next:

- **Ideas and feedback:** open an [Idea or Feedback issue](https://github.com/GTStagg/project-eyas/issues/new?template=idea.yaml). Describe the problem you're trying to solve; a description is more useful than a patch.
- **Bugs:** open a [Bug Report](https://github.com/GTStagg/project-eyas/issues/new?template=bug.yaml).
- **Questions:** open a [Question](https://github.com/GTStagg/project-eyas/issues/new?template=question.yaml).
- **Security problems:** report them privately, as described in the [security policy](../SECURITY.md#reporting), never in a public issue.
- **Problems in the MCP server's Falcon tools** that also happen outside Eyas belong in [eyas-mcp](https://github.com/GTStagg/eyas-mcp/issues).

Never include API credentials, tenant data or customer data in an issue.

Eyas is MIT licensed, so you're free to fork it and change it for your own organization.
